{{short description|Theorem in number theory}}
{{no footnotes|date=April 2016}}
In [[algebraic number theory]], the '''Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether theorem''' states that a [[central simple algebra]] over an [[algebraic number field]] ''K'' which splits over every [[local field|completion]] ''K''<sub>''v''</sub> is a [[matrix ring|matrix algebra]] over ''K''. The theorem is an example of a [[local-global principle]] in [[algebraic number theory]] and 
leads to a complete description of finite-dimensional [[division algebras]] over algebraic number fields in terms of their [[Hasse invariant of an algebra|local invariants]]. It was proved independently by [[Richard Brauer]], [[Helmut Hasse]], and [[Emmy Noether]] and by [[Abraham Adrian Albert]].

== Statement of the theorem ==

Let ''A'' be a [[central simple algebra]] of rank ''d'' over an [[algebraic number field]] ''K''. Suppose that for any [[valuation (algebra)|valuation]] ''v'', ''A'' splits over the corresponding local field ''K''<sub>''v''</sub>:

: <math> A\otimes_K K_v \simeq M_d(K_v). </math>

Then ''A'' is isomorphic to the matrix algebra ''M''<sub>''d''</sub>(''K'').

== Applications ==

Using the theory of [[Brauer group]], one shows that two central simple algebras ''A'' and ''B'' over an algebraic number field ''K'' are isomorphic over ''K'' if and only if their completions ''A''<sub>''v''</sub> and ''B''<sub>''v''</sub> are isomorphic over the completion ''K''<sub>''v''</sub> for every ''v''.

Together with the [[Grunwald–Wang theorem]], the Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether theorem implies that every central simple algebra over an algebraic number field is ''cyclic'', i.e. can be obtained by an explicit construction from a [[cyclic extension|cyclic field extension]] ''L''/''K'' .
